display.title: Episode 193: The Secret of the Empty Fireplace (Rosh Hashanah)
display.summary_short: A pre-Rosh Hashanah show: why it is the 'head' of the year, Shema with a Beis Rivkah student, the young Tzemach Tzedek in the fireplace, and the sounds of the shofar.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on 24 Elul 5745, the week before Rosh Hashanah 5746. Uncle Yossi explains, from the Mitteler Rebbe's sefer Ateres Rosh, why the day is called Rosh Hashanah, the head of the year, and not just its beginning: like the head of the body, it gives life to every day of the coming year, so we must be extra careful how we daven and behave. He also explains Selichos. After the Hakochainik march and a sponsor message, a nine-year-old Beis Rivkah student talks about her learning and leads the Shema. For the Tzemach Tzedek's birthday on Erev Rosh Hashanah, story time tells how nine-year-old Menachem Mendel, too young to join his grandfather the Alter Rebbe's lessons, hid in the empty fireplace to listen. One cold evening the fire was lit; he was pulled out motionless and revived when the Alter Rebbe laid his hand on his head. A guest rabbi then blows the tekiah, shevarim and teruah on the shofar, and Uncle Yossi gives the Rosh Hashanah schedule: candles on Sunday evening and the shofar on Monday and Tuesday.
display.lesson: Rosh Hashanah is the head of the whole year, so how we act on it shapes every day that follows; and love Torah so much that you will do anything to learn it.
